decisions.summary: read only the question fragments and their notes, never the assembled or citations pages

decisions.summary: a guess item is each sentence of visible text carrying GUESS or GUESSES; lower-case guess is not a label
decisions.why: FR-002(a), the comment edge case, SC-001 and the spec's edge case naming the plural

decisions.summary: an absence item is each notes li carrying 'no publicly readable source', with its search record and claim; 'settled' makes it absence-settled
GROUNDS notes and CONVENTION or DEVIATION labels are not items
decisions.why: the spec's edge case names both

decisions.summary: route (a) a class's Entry:; route (b) one hop of links from a question a class names
decisions.why: FR-003 and US2 define these two routes

decisions.summary: route (c) matches an engine .py line on the anchor or the heading's question up to its '?', with no length floor
decisions.why: FR-003's 'its heading or its anchor' as written (confirmed round 2); R5 now counts six short headings, three with no engine hit, eight hits all citations - the correction changes no conclusion

decisions.summary: make open-questions prints counts first, then the list, text only
outside the record: tracked text files under the skill less research/, tests/, the three tooling logs and binaries; each line carrying the whole word GUESS or GUESSES is an item
decisions.why: round 2 item confirmed: plan.md lines 36-37 now read 'the whole word GUESS or its plural GUESSES (as D2)', matching FR-007's 'every GUESS label' and the spec's plural edge case; the five GUESSES lines outside the record (compound.py 568/643, pondstock.py 8/25, county-magistracy-example.notes.md 24; git grep -w, this review) are now in scope, and scripts/_open_questions.py:38 _GUESS = GUESS(?:ES)? already reads them
